questions.title: Delete duplicates, keep the row with the smallest id
questions.given: person(id, email)
questions.answer:
DELETE FROM person
WHERE id IN (
  SELECT id FROM (
    SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY id) AS rn
    FROM person) t
  WHERE rn > 1);

questions.title: Trap: row counts for INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL join
questions.given: A(x) = 1,1,2,NULL B(x) = 1,1,NULL join on A.x = B.x
questions.answer:
-- INNER = 4 (each 1 in A matches both 1s in B: 2 x 2)
-- LEFT = 6 (4 + unmatched 2 + unmatched NULL)
-- RIGHT = 5 (4 + unmatched NULL in B)
-- FULL = 7 (4 + 2 from A + 1 from B)
questions.note: Duplicates multiply. NULL never equals NULL, so NULLs never match. Very commonly asked.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE A(x INT); INSERT INTO A VALUES (1),(1),(2),(NULL);
CREATE TABLE B(x INT); INSERT INTO B VALUES (1),(1),(NULL);

questions.title: Volume alert: days with less than half the usual rows
questions.given: daily_counts(d, row_count); 'usual' means the average of the 7 days before
questions.answer:
SELECT d, row_count, ROUND(prev_avg, 1) AS prev_avg
FROM (
  SELECT d, row_count,
         AVG(row_count) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_avg,
         COUNT(*)      OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_days
  FROM daily_counts) t
WHERE prev_days = 7 AND row_count < 0.5 * prev_avg;
questions.note: The window must end at 1 PRECEDING so today is not part of its own baseline. Require a full 7 days of history, or the first days alert on noise.
questions.ref:
SELECT d, row_count, ROUND(prev_avg, 1) AS prev_avg
FROM (
  SELECT d, row_count,
         AVG(row_count) OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_avg,
         COUNT(*)      OVER (ORDER BY d ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING) AS prev_days
  FROM daily_counts) t
WHERE prev_days = 7 AND row_count < 0.5 * prev_avg;

questions.title: Orphan check: orders whose customer does not exist
questions.given: orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date), customers(customer_id); count orphans per day
questions.answer:
SELECT o.order_date, COUNT(*) AS orphans
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL AND o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.order_date
ORDER BY o.order_date;
questions.note: Separate two problems: a customer_id that points nowhere (orphan, often a late dimension) and a missing customer_id (a NULL, a different quality rule). Reporting them together hides the cause.
questions.ref:
SELECT o.order_date, COUNT(*) AS orphans
FROM orders o
LEFT JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL AND o.customer_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY o.order_date
ORDER BY o.order_date;

questions.title: Schema drift: columns added, removed or retyped
questions.given: expected_schema(col, data_type) and actual_schema(col, data_type)
questions.answer:
SELECT COALESCE(e.col, a.col) AS col,
       CASE WHEN a.col IS NULL THEN 'removed'
            WHEN e.col IS NULL THEN 'added'
            ELSE 'type changed' END AS change,
       e.data_type AS expected_type, a.data_type AS actual_type
FROM expected_schema e
FULL OUTER JOIN actual_schema a ON a.col = e.col
WHERE e.col IS NULL OR a.col IS NULL OR e.data_type <> a.data_type
ORDER BY col;
questions.note: FULL OUTER JOIN shows both sides of a difference in one query. Run a check like this in bronze before silver jobs, so drift fails loudly instead of loading NULLs.
questions.ref:
SELECT COALESCE(e.col, a.col) AS col,
       CASE WHEN a.col IS NULL THEN 'removed'
            WHEN e.col IS NULL THEN 'added'
            ELSE 'type changed' END AS change,
       e.data_type AS expected_type, a.data_type AS actual_type
FROM expected_schema e
FULL OUTER JOIN actual_schema a ON a.col = e.col
WHERE e.col IS NULL OR a.col IS NULL OR e.data_type <> a.data_type
ORDER BY col;

questions.title: Flatten nested data: one row per item with the customer's city
questions.given: raw_orders(order_id, payload) where payload is a struct with customer {id, city} and items, a list of {sku, qty}, as it lands after parsing JSON or Avro
questions.answer:
SELECT o.order_id,
       o.payload.customer.city AS city,
       t.item.sku AS sku,
       t.item.qty AS qty
FROM raw_orders o,
     UNNEST(o.payload.items) AS t(item)
ORDER BY o.order_id, sku;
questions.note: Read nested fields with dot paths and turn the array into rows with UNNEST (explode in Spark, FLATTEN in Snowflake). Orders with an empty array disappear; use a LEFT JOIN with UNNEST if the business needs them kept.
questions.ref:
SELECT o.order_id,
       o.payload.customer.city AS city,
       t.item.sku AS sku,
       t.item.qty AS qty
FROM raw_orders o,
     UNNEST(o.payload.items) AS t(item)
ORDER BY o.order_id, sku;

questions.title: Customer lifetime metrics in one pass
questions.given: orders(order_id, customer_id, order_date, amount, status); only status 'paid' counts as revenue
questions.answer:
SELECT customer_id,
       MIN(order_date) AS first_order,
       MAX(order_date) AS last_order,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid') AS paid_orders,
       COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid'), 0) AS revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY customer_id;
questions.note: Conditional aggregates compute several metrics in one scan instead of one query per metric. COALESCE turns 'no paid orders' into 0 instead of NULL.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE orders(order_id INT, customer_id INT, order_date DATE, amount INT, status VARCHAR);

questions.ref:
SELECT customer_id,
       MIN(order_date) AS first_order,
       MAX(order_date) AS last_order,
       COUNT(*) AS orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid') AS paid_orders,
       COALESCE(SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status = 'paid'), 0) AS revenue
FROM orders
GROUP BY customer_id
ORDER BY customer_id;

questions.title: Fact load with an 'unknown' member for missing products
questions.given: order_lines(line_id, sku, qty, price); dim_product(product_key, sku); unknown products must get product_key -1
questions.answer:
SELECT l.line_id,
       COALESCE(p.product_key, -1) AS product_key,
       l.qty * l.price AS revenue
FROM order_lines l
LEFT JOIN dim_product p ON p.sku = l.sku
ORDER BY l.line_id;
questions.note: A fact table must not lose rows because a dimension is late or wrong. LEFT JOIN and map misses to an 'unknown' member, then report how many rows hit it.
questions.ref:
SELECT l.line_id,
       COALESCE(p.product_key, -1) AS product_key,
       l.qty * l.price AS revenue
FROM order_lines l
LEFT JOIN dim_product p ON p.sku = l.sku
ORDER BY l.line_id;

questions.title: Deduplicate with a tie-breaker on source priority
questions.given: customer_raw(id, email, updated_at, source); when updated_at ties, source 'crm' beats 'app' beats 'import'
questions.answer:
SELECT id, email, source
FROM customer_raw
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY id
  ORDER BY updated_at DESC,
           CASE source WHEN 'crm' THEN 1 WHEN 'app' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END) = 1
ORDER BY id;
questions.note: Without a tie-breaker, ROW_NUMBER picks a random winner and the pipeline gives different answers on each run. Always make the ORDER BY deterministic.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE customer_raw(id INT, email VARCHAR, updated_at TIMESTAMP, source VARCHAR);
INSERT INTO customer_raw VALUES (1,'a@x.in','2026-03-01 10:00','app'),(1,'a@crm.in','2026-03-01 10:00','crm'),(2,'b@x.in','2026-03-01 09:00','import'),(2,'b@new.in','2026-03-02 09:00','import'),(3,'c@app.in','2026-03-01 08:00','app'),(3,'c@imp.in','2026-03-01 08:00','import');
questions.ref:
SELECT id, email, source
FROM customer_raw
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY id
  ORDER BY updated_at DESC,
           CASE source WHEN 'crm' THEN 1 WHEN 'app' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END) = 1
ORDER BY id;

questions.title: Change detection with a row hash
questions.given: staging(id, name, city) and target(id, name, city, row_hash) where row_hash = md5(name || '|' || city)
questions.answer:
SELECT s.id,
       CASE WHEN t.id IS NULL THEN 'new' ELSE 'changed' END AS change
FROM staging s
LEFT JOIN target t ON t.id = s.id
WHERE t.id IS NULL OR t.row_hash <> md5(s.name || '|' || s.city)
ORDER BY s.id;
questions.note: Comparing one hash is simpler than comparing every column, and it scales to wide tables. Use a separator so ('ab','c') and ('a','bc') do not hash the same, and COALESCE NULLs before hashing in real pipelines.
questions.ref:
SELECT s.id,
       CASE WHEN t.id IS NULL THEN 'new' ELSE 'changed' END AS change
FROM staging s
LEFT JOIN target t ON t.id = s.id
WHERE t.id IS NULL OR t.row_hash <> md5(s.name || '|' || s.city)
ORDER BY s.id;

questions.title: Rewrite a filter so partitions can be skipped
questions.given: events(event_id, ts) is partitioned by date; find events on 2026-03-02
questions.answer:
SELECT event_id
FROM events
WHERE ts >= TIMESTAMP '2026-03-02 00:00:00'
  AND ts <  TIMESTAMP '2026-03-03 00:00:00'
ORDER BY event_id;
questions.note: A function on the column (CAST, DATE(), YEAR()) hides the raw value from the planner, so it cannot prune partitions or use min/max statistics. A half-open range on the raw column gives the same rows and lets the engine skip files.
questions.ref:
SELECT event_id
FROM events
WHERE ts >= TIMESTAMP '2026-03-02 00:00:00'
  AND ts <  TIMESTAMP '2026-03-03 00:00:00'
ORDER BY event_id;
questions.starter:
-- Slow: the CAST hides ts from partition pruning
SELECT event_id
FROM events
WHERE CAST(ts AS DATE) = DATE '2026-03-02'

questions.title: Incremental load with an overlap window, without duplicates
questions.given: source(id, val, updated_at), target(id, val, updated_at), watermark 2026-03-02 10:00; reload 1 hour of overlap to catch late commits
questions.answer:
MERGE INTO target t
USING (SELECT * FROM source
       WHERE updated_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-03-02 10:00' - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) s
ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at > t.updated_at THEN
  UPDATE SET val = s.val, updated_at = s.updated_at
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (s.id, s.val, s.updated_at);
questions.note: Rows committed late can carry an updated_at just before the watermark. Re-reading a small overlap catches them, and MERGE makes the overlap safe: rows already loaded update in place instead of duplicating.
questions.ref:
MERGE INTO target t
USING (SELECT * FROM source
       WHERE updated_at > TIMESTAMP '2026-03-02 10:00' - INTERVAL 1 HOUR) s
ON t.id = s.id
WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at > t.updated_at THEN
  UPDATE SET val = s.val, updated_at = s.updated_at
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT VALUES (s.id, s.val, s.updated_at);
questions.check: SELECT * FROM target ORDER BY id

questions.title: Quality report: which rules each row breaks
questions.given: payments(id, amount, currency, paid_at); rules: amount > 0, currency in INR/USD, paid_at not NULL
questions.answer:
SELECT id,
       CONCAT_WS(', ',
         CASE WHEN amount <= 0 THEN 'amount' END,
         CASE WHEN currency NOT IN ('INR', 'USD') THEN 'currency' END,
         CASE WHEN paid_at IS NULL THEN 'paid_at' END) AS failed_rules
FROM payments
WHERE amount <= 0 OR currency NOT IN ('INR', 'USD') OR paid_at IS NULL
ORDER BY id;
questions.note: Listing every failed rule per row (not just pass/fail) makes quarantine tables useful: the owner sees what to fix. CONCAT_WS skips NULLs, so CASE without ELSE builds the list cleanly.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE payments(id INT, amount DECIMAL(10,2), currency VARCHAR, paid_at TIMESTAMP);
INSERT INTO payments VALUES (1,100,'INR','2026-03-01 10:00'),(2,-5,'INR','2026-03-01 11:00'),(3,20,'EUR',NULL),(4,0,'USD','2026-03-01 12:00'),(5,15,'USD','2026-03-01 12:30');
questions.ref:
SELECT id,
       CONCAT_WS(', ',
         CASE WHEN amount <= 0 THEN 'amount' END,
         CASE WHEN currency NOT IN ('INR', 'USD') THEN 'currency' END,
         CASE WHEN paid_at IS NULL THEN 'paid_at' END) AS failed_rules
FROM payments
WHERE amount <= 0 OR currency NOT IN ('INR', 'USD') OR paid_at IS NULL
ORDER BY id;

questions.title: Split a comma-separated tag column and count each tag
questions.given: articles(id, tags) where tags is text like 'sql, spark'
questions.answer:
SELECT LOWER(TRIM(tag)) AS tag, COUNT(*) AS articles
FROM articles, UNNEST(string_split(tags, ',')) AS t(tag)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY articles DESC, tag;
questions.note: Split, then normalise (TRIM and LOWER) before grouping, or 'sql', ' sql' and 'SQL' count as three tags. In a warehouse this becomes a bridge table: one row per article and tag.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE articles(id INT, tags VARCHAR);
INSERT INTO articles VALUES (1,'sql, spark'),(2,'spark,kafka'),(3,'SQL'),(4,NULL),(5,'kafka, sql ,dbt');

FROM articles, UNNEST(string_split(tags, ',')) AS t(tag)

questions.title: Running balance per account from a ledger
questions.given: ledger(account_id, ts, kind, amount) where kind is 'credit' or 'debit'
questions.answer:
SELECT account_id, ts, kind, amount,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END)
         OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY ts, amount
               ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS balance
FROM ledger
ORDER BY account_id, ts, amount;
questions.note: Sign the amount first, then run a cumulative SUM. Use ROWS (not the default RANGE) and a unique ORDER BY, or rows with the same timestamp get the same balance.
questions.ref:
SELECT account_id, ts, kind, amount,
       SUM(CASE WHEN kind = 'credit' THEN amount ELSE -amount END)
         OVER (PARTITION BY account_id ORDER BY ts, amount
               ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) AS balance
FROM ledger
ORDER BY account_id, ts, amount;

questions.title: Give new dimension rows surrogate keys after the current max
questions.given: dim_city(city_key, city) and new_cities(city), which may include cities already in the dimension
questions.answer:
INSERT INTO dim_city
SELECT (SELECT MAX(city_key) FROM dim_city) + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY city), city
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM new_cities) n
WHERE city NOT IN (SELECT city FROM dim_city);
questions.note: Keys continue after the current maximum, are assigned only to truly new members, and are deterministic (ORDER BY city). In Delta or Snowflake you would usually use an identity column, but interviewers like to see this done by hand.
questions.ref:
INSERT INTO dim_city
SELECT (SELECT MAX(city_key) FROM dim_city) + ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY city), city
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT city FROM new_cities) n
WHERE city NOT IN (SELECT city FROM dim_city);
questions.check: SELECT * FROM dim_city ORDER BY city_key

questions.title: Flag events that arrived after the watermark
questions.given: events(event_id, event_ts, arrived_ts); hourly windows close 1 hour after they end; count on-time and late events per window
questions.answer:
SELECT date_trunc('hour', event_ts) AS window_start,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE arrived_ts <= date_trunc('hour', event_ts) + INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AS on_time,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE arrived_ts >  date_trunc('hour', event_ts) + INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AS late
FROM events
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
questions.note: A window ends 1 hour after it starts and closes 1 hour after that, so the cut-off is window start + 2 hours. This is exactly what a streaming watermark does: late rows are dropped or sent to a side output.
questions.ref:
SELECT date_trunc('hour', event_ts) AS window_start,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE arrived_ts <= date_trunc('hour', event_ts) + INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AS on_time,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE arrived_ts >  date_trunc('hour', event_ts) + INTERVAL 2 HOUR) AS late
FROM events
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

questions.title: Find partitions that need compaction
questions.given: file_log(table_name, partition_date, file_name, size_mb); compact partitions with more than 3 files under 10 MB
questions.answer:
SELECT table_name, partition_date, COUNT(*) AS small_files, SUM(size_mb) AS small_mb
FROM file_log
WHERE size_mb < 10
GROUP BY table_name, partition_date
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
ORDER BY table_name, partition_date;
questions.note: Many small files slow every reader because each file costs an open and a metadata read. Filter to small files in WHERE, then keep partitions with too many in HAVING; OPTIMIZE (Delta) or rewrite_data_files (Iceberg) fixes them.
questions.ref:
SELECT table_name, partition_date, COUNT(*) AS small_files, SUM(size_mb) AS small_mb
FROM file_log
WHERE size_mb < 10
GROUP BY table_name, partition_date
HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
ORDER BY table_name, partition_date;

questions.title: Pivot event counts into a feature table
questions.given: events(user_id, event_type) with types 'view', 'click', 'purchase'; one row per user with a column per type
questions.answer:

       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type = 'view')     AS views,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type = 'click')    AS clicks,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE event_type = 'purchase') AS purchases
FROM events
GROUP BY user_id
ORDER BY user_id;

questions.title: Reporting path for each employee, top to bottom
questions.given: emp(id, name, manager_id); build a path like 'Kavya > Arjun > Neha'
questions.answer:
WITH RECURSIVE r AS (
  SELECT id, name, name AS path FROM emp WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, r.path || ' > ' || e.name
  FROM emp e JOIN r ON e.manager_id = r.id
)
SELECT id, path FROM r ORDER BY id;
questions.note: Start from the root (manager_id IS NULL) and append one level per recursion step. In production add a depth limit so a cycle in bad data cannot loop forever.

INSERT INTO emp VALUES (1,'Kavya',NULL),(2,'Arjun',1),(3,'Neha',2),(4,'Sam',2),(5,'Lina',1),(6,'Omar',5);
questions.ref:

  SELECT id, name, name AS path FROM emp WHERE manager_id IS NULL
  UNION ALL
  SELECT e.id, e.name, r.path || ' > ' || e.name
  FROM emp e JOIN r ON e.manager_id = r.id
)
SELECT id, path FROM r ORDER BY id;

questions.title: Possible duplicate payments within 5 minutes
questions.given: payments(id, customer_id, amount, paid_at); same customer and amount within 5 minutes of the previous payment
questions.answer:
SELECT id, prev_id, customer_id, amount
FROM (
  SELECT id, customer_id, amount, paid_at,
         LAG(id)      OVER w AS prev_id,
         LAG(paid_at) OVER w AS prev_at
  FROM payments
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY customer_id, amount ORDER BY paid_at)) t
WHERE paid_at - prev_at <= INTERVAL 5 MINUTE
ORDER BY id;
questions.note: Partition by everything that must match (customer and amount), order by time, and compare with the previous row. The boundary matters: payment 7 is exactly 5 minutes later and counts.
questions.ref:
SELECT id, prev_id, customer_id, amount
FROM (
  SELECT id, customer_id, amount, paid_at,
         LAG(id)      OVER w AS prev_id,
         LAG(paid_at) OVER w AS prev_at
  FROM payments
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY customer_id, amount ORDER BY paid_at)) t
WHERE paid_at - prev_at <= INTERVAL 5 MINUTE
ORDER BY id;

questions.title: Fill missing days with zero for every store
questions.given: sales(store_id, d, amount) for 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-04; stores(store_id); one row per store per day
questions.answer:
SELECT s.store_id, CAST(g.d AS DATE) AS d, COALESCE(SUM(x.amount), 0) AS amount
FROM stores s
CROSS JOIN generate_series(DATE '2026-03-01', DATE '2026-03-04', INTERVAL 1 DAY) g(d)
LEFT JOIN sales x ON x.store_id = s.store_id AND x.d = CAST(g.d AS DATE)
GROUP BY s.store_id, g.d
ORDER BY s.store_id, d;
questions.note: Charts and moving averages break when days are missing. Cross join entities with a date spine, LEFT JOIN the facts, and COALESCE to 0.
questions.ref:
SELECT s.store_id, CAST(g.d AS DATE) AS d, COALESCE(SUM(x.amount), 0) AS amount
FROM stores s
CROSS JOIN generate_series(DATE '2026-03-01', DATE '2026-03-04', INTERVAL 1 DAY) g(d)
LEFT JOIN sales x ON x.store_id = s.store_id AND x.d = CAST(g.d AS DATE)
GROUP BY s.store_id, g.d
ORDER BY s.store_id, d;

questions.title: Rerun-safe daily aggregate for one partition
questions.given: orders(order_id, d, amount); daily_revenue(d, revenue) already holds a stale row for 2026-03-02; rebuild only that date
questions.note: An INSERT on its own doubles the row on every rerun. Delete-then-insert (or INSERT OVERWRITE a partition, or MERGE) makes the job idempotent, which is what lets an orchestrator retry it safely.

questions.title: Turn SCD2 history into change events
questions.given: dim_customer(cust_id, city, valid_from); list every move with from_city, to_city and the date
questions.answer:
SELECT cust_id, from_city, city AS to_city, valid_from AS moved_on
FROM (
  SELECT cust_id, city, valid_from,
         LAG(city) OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS from_city
  FROM dim_customer) t
WHERE from_city IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY cust_id, moved_on;
questions.note: Each version after the first is a change event. LAG gives the previous value; the first version has no previous city and is not a move.
questions.setup:
CREATE TABLE dim_customer(cust_id INT, city VARCHAR, valid_from DATE);
INSERT INTO dim_customer VALUES (1,'Pune','2025-01-01'),(1,'Mumbai','2025-06-01'),(1,'Pune','2025-09-01'),(2,'Delhi','2025-01-01'),(3,'Goa','2025-02-01'),(3,'Chennai','2025-03-01');

SELECT cust_id, from_city, city AS to_city, valid_from AS moved_on
FROM (
  SELECT cust_id, city, valid_from,
         LAG(city) OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS from_city
  FROM dim_customer) t
WHERE from_city IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY cust_id, moved_on;

questions.title: Reconcile amounts between source and target per day
questions.given: src(d, amount) and tgt(d, amount); show days whose totals differ by more than 0.01, or exist on one side only
questions.answer:
SELECT COALESCE(s.d, t.d) AS d, s.total AS src_total, t.total AS tgt_total
FROM (SELECT d, SUM(amount) AS total FROM src GROUP BY d) s
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT d, SUM(amount) AS total FROM tgt GROUP BY d) t ON t.d = s.d
WHERE s.d IS NULL OR t.d IS NULL OR ABS(s.total - t.total) > 0.01
ORDER BY d;
questions.note: Aggregate each side first, then FULL OUTER JOIN, or a day missing on one side disappears from the check. A small tolerance avoids false alarms from rounding.
questions.ref:
SELECT COALESCE(s.d, t.d) AS d, s.total AS src_total, t.total AS tgt_total
FROM (SELECT d, SUM(amount) AS total FROM src GROUP BY d) s
FULL OUTER JOIN (SELECT d, SUM(amount) AS total FROM tgt GROUP BY d) t ON t.d = s.d
WHERE s.d IS NULL OR t.d IS NULL OR ABS(s.total - t.total) > 0.01
ORDER BY d;

questions.title: Customers who changed city more than once in a year
questions.given: dim_customer(cust_id, city, valid_from); count moves per customer in 2025, keep those with 2 or more
questions.answer:
SELECT cust_id, COUNT(*) AS moves_2025
FROM (
  SELECT cust_id, valid_from,
         LAG(city) OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS prev_city
  FROM dim_customer) t
WHERE prev_city IS NOT NULL
  AND valid_from >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND valid_from < DATE '2026-01-01'

questions.note: Compute LAG over the full history before filtering by year, or a customer's first version inside 2025 looks like a non-move. Window first, then filter, then aggregate.
questions.ref:
SELECT cust_id, COUNT(*) AS moves_2025
FROM (
  SELECT cust_id, valid_from,
         LAG(city) OVER (PARTITION BY cust_id ORDER BY valid_from) AS prev_city
  FROM dim_customer) t
WHERE prev_city IS NOT NULL
  AND valid_from >= DATE '2025-01-01' AND valid_from < DATE '2026-01-01'
GROUP BY cust_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2
ORDER BY cust_id;
